obligations.note: In ApplicantValidator.checkIncome the change replaces `Mask.npi(value)` with the raw `value` in a `log.warn` call. Annual income is NPI (ENC-1 statement; `mortgage.npi_fields` includes `annual_income`), so a rejected income value now reaches the application log unmasked.

No exception in the register covers this deviation. EXC-0167 (mortgage.logging) is scoped to a legacy import job writing a masked last-4 of the bank account number, which is a different component and a different behaviour. The LOG-1 deviation therefore has no approved exception.
Ticket CHG-25973 is standard and approved by grace.kim (change_manager) on 2026-10-10, before the change opened. Its component mortgage.cases covers ApplicantValidator.java, the only file changed.
The code_review approval is from declan.farrell, who holds change_approver for baseline-mortgage and is a different person from the author, priya.raman.
The approval names the head commit 4f1da65b, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json reports success on head 4f1da65b, run by ci-runner-01 on 2026-10-12. The attached JUnit reports, however, are timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time, and come from host dev-laptop-7.local. They therefore cannot be tied to this CI run. Their passing `rejectsMalformedNpiWithoutLoggingIt` and `sampledFlowsDoNotLogNpi` results also say nothing about the new raw-income log, since the LOG-1 control test is only a sample.
The only touched component is mortgage.cases, which is not marked security_sensitive, so no security review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not flagged as an emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
Ledger entries cover Approvals, Underwriting, Policy and payments code, none of which this change touches. No accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change removes NPI masking from the annual-income validation log message, so raw income values are written to application logs. This violates LOG-1, and no exception in the register covers it. The description's claim of 'diagnostics' does not excuse logging unmasked NPI. The CI evidence is also inconsistent: the reports are dated after the review time and come from a personal machine. The change is rejected.
